_meta.title: Z3 INSTRUMENT ID: Gemini listens to the other stem

inputs.value:
Look at the picture (the album cover) and read the analysis of the song below.

SONG ANALYSIS
Instruments heard in the full song (from a listening model):
Instruments heard in the Demucs 'other' stem (everything except vocals, drums, bass):
Loudness of each Demucs stem per 10 second window (LUFS; quieter than about -40 LUFS means that stem is essentially silent there):

HOW TO MATCH
- Each instrument family maps to a stem: voice -> vocals stem (<Audio 1>); drum kit and drums -> drums stem (<Audio 2>); bass guitar, upright bass, double bass -> bass stem; every other instrument (guitars, keys, piano, horns, strings, harmonica, percussion other than the kit) -> other stem.
- Listening models often confuse instruments inside one family, so match by FAMILY: horns (trumpet, cornet, saxophone, trombone, clarinet, brass, horn section); guitars (acoustic, electric, steel, banjo, mandolin, ukulele); keys (piano, organ, synth, synthesizer, keyboard, harmonium); bowed strings (violin, fiddle, viola, cello, string section); basses (electric bass, upright bass, double bass). A visible trumpeter plays a heard saxophone or horn line, and so on.
- An instrument counts as HEARD when the listening lists name it or another member of its family AND its stem is louder than about -40 LUFS in at least one window. Trust the loudness numbers over the listening lists when they disagree.
- A visible player whose instrument is HEARD plays along with that sound (name the sound: the drums, the bass notes, the trumpet line, the guitar chords, and so on).
- A visible player whose instrument is NOT heard moves only to the beat: their hands keep a gentle, steady pulse on the instrument with each drum beat.
- A heard instrument with no visible player goes only into the MUSIC slot and the HEARD_NO_PLAYER list; it is never given to a person.
- Singer: if the vocals stem is louder than about -40 LUFS in some window, choose exactly one singer: the person at a microphone; if no microphone is visible and the cover shows exactly one performer whose mouth is free, that performer sings; if no microphone is visible and the cover shows two or more performers, choose none. A performer with a wind instrument at the lips is never the singer. If vocals are silent in every window, choose none.

FILL THESE SLOTS
[MOOD]
two or three capital words for the feel, like WARM SWING or SOFT FOLK GLOW
[/MOOD]
[STYLE]
the art style and setting as one noun phrase starting with "a" or "an", like: an etched-print sepia illustration of a 1940s club stage
[/STYLE]
[SHOT]
one noun phrase for what the cover shows, like: a four-man band under five stage lamps
[/SHOT]
[PALETTE]
the colours and light of the cover as a short phrase, like: sepia etched print, warm cream light cones on a dark stage
[/PALETTE]
[SUBJECTS]
one line per visible person, left to right, in this form:
<Subject 1> is THE ROLE: position in the frame, two or three visible details of looks and clothes, the instrument or microphone they hold.
(ROLE is a short capitalised job name such as SINGER, BASSIST, DRUMMER, GUITARIST, TRUMPETER, PIANIST; the singer, if any, is called THE SINGER.)
then one last line for the scenery:
<Subject N> is THE WORLD: the visible lights, scenery and objects, including any instrument that nobody plays.
[/SUBJECTS]
[WORLD_MOTION]
four to seven slow, subtle motions for the visible scenery only, separated by semicolons, like: the five stage lamps glow and pulse slowly; the heavy curtains sway slowly; the cymbals shimmer softly
[/WORLD_MOTION]
[SINGER_LINE]
If there is a singer, write exactly this sentence with the pronoun fixed to match the person:
THE SINGER is the one singer and sings <Audio 1>: lips on each sung syllable, lips and jaw shaping each word, mouth opening moderately, restrained, his head drifting slowly in small turns on held notes, shoulders still; between lines the lips rest together in a smile. Everyone else keeps lips together.
If there is no singer, write exactly this sentence:
<Audio 1> is the voice of the song, heard from off the cover; every person on the cover keeps lips together in a calm, happy expression the whole time.
[/SINGER_LINE]
[PLAYERS]
one line for each visible person other than the singer, in this form (fit the hands to the real instrument):
THE ROLE: on each <sound of their instrument> <the hand> <the playing motion>; <the other hand> <a steady supporting motion>; head calm, shoulders still, the motion in the hands.
For the drummer use: on each kick of <Audio 2> his foot presses the kick pedal; on each snare his right stick lands on the snare; on every first beat his right stick taps the cymbal; head calm, his motion in his hands and foot.
For a player whose instrument is not heard: THE ROLE: the hands keep a gentle, steady pulse on the instrument with each drum beat; head calm, shoulders still.
If the singer is the only person, write one line about the singer's free hand, like: THE SINGER's free hand lifts a little on each new line and settles.
[/PLAYERS]
[WORLD_ANSWER]
three or four links between the music and the scenery, separated by semicolons, like: on each kick the five lamps brighten a little and settle; on each snare the cymbals shimmer with light; with the bass notes the curtains sway slowly
[/WORLD_ANSWER]
[SOUNDSCAPE]
the room sound of this setting as a short phrase, like: a smoky 1940s club, glasses clinking, a happy crowd.
[/SOUNDSCAPE]
[MUSIC]
the genre and tempo feel, then one short sentence per HEARD instrument, like: a swinging rock-and-roll anthem. The drums driving. The plucked upright bass. The trumpet line. The voice.
[/MUSIC]
[INSTRUMENTS]
one line per heard sound and one line per visible player, in this form:
HEARD <instrument> | stem <vocals/drums/bass/other> | windows <1,2,3> | player <ROLE or (heard, no player on the cover)>
PLAYER <ROLE> | instrument <visible instrument> | <plays its own sound (stem name) or moves to the beat only (instrument unheard)>
[/INSTRUMENTS]
[HEARD_NO_PLAYER]
a comma separated list of heard instruments that have no visible player, each followed by "(heard, no player on the cover)"; if every heard instrument has a player, write: every heard instrument has a player on the cover
[/HEARD_NO_PLAYER]

_meta.title: Z2 AUTO-PROMPT request (cover rules + heard lists + loudness)

inputs.value:
You fill the slots of a FIXED video-prompt template for MiniMax H3, which animates an album cover into a 30 second music performance with a locked-off camera.
Hard rules:
1. Describe only what is visible in the picture. Count the people carefully. Every person you name must be clearly visible; every instrument you name must be clearly visible in the picture. Empty instruments with nobody playing them are scenery, never a player.
2. Exactly one singer or none (rule for choosing below).
3. Write every slot in positive wording. The slot text must contain zero negation words: avoid the words no, not, never, nothing, without, none, nor, neither, nobody, cannot, and every contraction ending in n't. Say what happens, never what is absent.
4. Use plain English, present tense, short clauses separated by semicolons.
5. Output exactly the tagged blocks requested, each opening tag and closing tag on its own line, and nothing outside them.
